subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing recurring-cron cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving current behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast recurring jobs?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and deliberate opt-in schedule rejection/pacing behavior, which repository policy treats as a compatibility-sensitive maintainer decision rather than a pure bug fix.

options.title: Accept After Narrow Fixes
options.body: Keep the default-off guardrail, but exempt non-recurring schedule kinds and refresh generated docs before merge.

options.title: Narrow To Advisory Behavior
options.body: Decline enforcement for now and revive warning-only feedback if maintainers do not want configured schedule rejection or pacing.

options.title: Defer Core Config
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a broader cron/operator guardrail policy.

recommendation.title: Accept After Narrow Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the default-off guardrail, but exempt non-recurring schedule kinds and refresh generated docs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned on the live PR and has recent history in the cron update/re-arm surface this config changes.
